## China competition fears trigger rout in Korean memory stocks; SK Hynix falls below US listing price

Chinese displacement risk is the key bear case for HBM-exposed names; SK Hynix trading below its US listing price signals the market is re-rating the export-control moat materially downward. Sustained pressure here would challenge AI memory pricing assumptions and could spill into US-listed beneficiaries of HBM demand.

- Asian semiconductor equities sold off sharply as investor concern mounted over Chinese competition in AI-related chips.
- SK Hynix fell below its US listing price — a psychologically significant level — as the selloff accelerated.
- Samsung Electronics also declined materially, with both names leading losses across the Korean memory complex.
- US chip stocks extended losses in sympathy, indicating contagion from the Korean names into the broader AI trade.
- The catalyst is fear of China gaining competitive ground in the HBM and broader AI memory supply chain, not a company-specific fundamental event.
